userStories.title: API and protocol accept ACP agents on every thread kind
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Accept Claude Code, Codex and Cursor ACP backends on every thread kind and carry bounded discovery offers through the API.

**Motivation** — To get code changes a person must dispatch a fleet RUN.

**Approach** — A thread pinned to a runner whose agent became unavailable fails placement with the existing `thread_backend` misfit.

Target: `'claude' | 'codex' | 'cursor'`. Target: `{ native: string[]; acp: ThreadAgent[]; acpOffers?: ThreadAcpOffer[] }`; `acp` lists the agents that are launchable AND logged in (placement keeps `acp.includes(agent)`); new `ThreadAcpOffer { agent: ThreadAgent; launchable: boolean; loggedIn: boolean | null; models: string[]; efforts: string[] }` (`loggedIn: null` = not probed or probe failed).

Target: agents add `cursor`; an optional `acpOffers` (at most `THREAD_LIMITS.maxAcpAgents` entries, each agent at most once, `models` at most `maxNativeModels` ids matching `ACP_MODEL_ID_RE`, `efforts` at most 8 entries matching `^[a-z0-9_-]{1,32}$`) is kept when valid and dropped when malformed, the rest of the report still accepted. ACP model ids in `acpOffers` and in an `acp` create backend are checked with it; native model ids keep `MODEL_ID_RE`.

Target: `acp` agent `claude|codex|cursor` on every kind. `RunnerSummaryDto.threadBackends` and web `RunnerThreadBackends` (`apps/web/lib/thread-types.ts`, `lib/fleet-types.ts`) carry a valid `acpOffers` through. The web mirror work is consumed in US-011.

**Scope** — In: protocol exports and API runtime mirror, capability parsing, normalized backend types/validation, runner summary projection, existing ACP placement rule and regression specs. Update PROJECT/WORKSPACE input tests that currently refuse ACP; update capabilities-thread.spec.ts's exactly-two-keys expectation and runner-summary.dto.spec.ts projection assertions. Out: host probes (US-002), session opening/assign parsing (US-003), modes and permissions (US-004), web forms (US-011). ACP agents other than `claude`, `codex` and `cursor` (nax-agent-acp also knows `gemini`, `opencode`, `pi`).

**Interface** — `ThreadAgent`: `'claude' | 'codex' | 'cursor'`; `ThreadBackends`: `{ native: string[]; acp: ThreadAgent[]; acpOffers?: ThreadAcpOffer[] }`; `ThreadAcpOffer { agent: ThreadAgent; launchable: boolean; loggedIn: boolean | null; models: string[]; efforts: string[] }`. New `ACP_MODEL_ID_RE = /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:\/@=,\[\]-]{0,127}$/` (protocol constant, mirrored at runtime in `thread-jobs.ts`). API imports fleet-protocol as types only; mirror the regex locally.

**Verification** — Extend the existing normalizer, capabilities, DTO and placement unit specs with strict unknown-agent/unknown-key rejection and malformed-offer degradation; retain native-model regression behavior.

userStories.title: Runner advertises its ACP agents
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Discover launchable/logged-in ACP agents with their offered models and efforts and advertise them through production runner sync.

**Motivation** — `nax chat` already offers all four agents with read/ask/full modes on one machine.

**Approach** — `probeAcpAgents` checks `claude`, `codex`, `cursor` in parallel:
`launchCandidateKind(agent, env)` decides `launchable` (local binary or `npx` fallback); for a launchable agent it opens a tool-less, memory-only `ask` session through `acpBackend` with `initializeTimeoutMs` 20000 and a 20 s overall timeout, reads `backend.capabilities.offeredModels` / `offeredEfforts`, drops ids failing `ACP_MODEL_ID_RE` (models, capped at 32) or the effort pattern (capped at 8), and closes the session; `AGENT_SESSION_AUTH_REQUIRED` gives `loggedIn: false`; a timeout or other error gives `loggedIn: null` with empty lists, and a session that opens after its timeout is closed when it settles. A thread pinned to a runner whose agent became unavailable fails placement with the existing `thread_backend` misfit.

`NaxCapabilityProbe` (`nax-probe.ts:145-180`). Target: `NaxProbeDeps.acpProbe?: AcpAgentProbe`; when present its result fills `acp` and `acpOffers` (omitted when empty); when absent `acp` stays `[]`. `DaemonOptions` (`apps/runner/src/daemon/daemon.ts`) gains `acpProbe?: AcpAgentProbe`, passed to `createCapabilityProbe`; the `run` command (`apps/runner/src/commands/run.ts`) passes the real `probeAcpAgents`. Other `startDaemon` callers (tests) get no ACP probe.

**Scope** — In: exact @nathapp/nax-agent-acp 0.91.7 dependency and lockfile update, new acp-agent-probe source/spec, dependency injection through capability construction/daemon/run command, bounded report integration and concurrent timeout cleanup. Existing @nathapp/nax-agent is already 0.91.7. Update nax-probe.spec.ts to distinguish absent, injected and failed probe behavior; exercise a real injected daemon sync without host logins. Out: actual thread session opening (US-003), threadModes reporting (US-006). The central credential vault (#371): credentials stay on the runner (the agent's own login for ACP, the nax auth store or its existing `credentials.source: exec` config for native). Any sandbox for ACP agents: they run unsandboxed on the runner host in every mode, as in `nax chat` (user ruling). Bumping `@nathapp/nax-agent` beyond `0.91.7`.

**Interface** — `NaxProbeDeps.acpProbe?: AcpAgentProbe`; `DaemonOptions.acpProbe?: AcpAgentProbe`; `ThreadAcpOffer { agent: ThreadAgent; launchable: boolean; loggedIn: boolean | null; models: string[]; efforts: string[] }`; dependency entry `"@nathapp/nax-agent-acp": "0.91.7"`. Use `launchCandidateKind` and `acpBackend` from `@nathapp/nax-agent-acp/client` 0.91.7. Opens inherit the accepted unsandboxed ACP host behavior.

**Verification** — Inject launch checks, backend/session creation and timers; prove concurrent starts, all outcomes, session closure even after timeout, and run-command-to-daemon-to-sync wiring. Preserve the operator's static capability override and the no-probe default in other daemon tests.

userStories.title: Runner opens ACP thread sessions
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Open ACP threads through the injected ACP backend factory with declared thread tools and accept Cursor assignments.

**Motivation** — `nax chat` already offers all four agents with read/ask/full modes on one machine.

**Approach** — Opening an `acp` thread uses `acpBackend({ agent, allowUnsandboxed: true, inheritEnv: true, model?, effort? })` with the same session options as native (workdir, instructions, declared tools, transcript store, approval timeout, turn timeout 900 s).

ACP agents run unsandboxed on the runner host in every mode, exactly as `nax chat` opens them (`acpBackend({ agent, allowUnsandboxed: true, inheritEnv: true, model?, effort? })`, no sandbox option). Accepted by the user. nax#2444 is done: `acpBackend` serves the session's declared tools over its loopback tool host, so ACP agents get koda's thread tools and are allowed on REPO, PROJECT and WORKSPACE threads.

`ThreadSessionFactory.open`. Target: opens `acp` through an injectable `acpBackend` factory (factory dependency `acpBackend`, default the package's). Assign parser (`apps/runner/src/supervisor/assign-parser.ts:34-60,320-337`). Target: accepts `cursor` (ACP model by `ACP_MODEL_ID_RE`).

**Scope** — In: ACP factory dependency with production default, native/ACP backend branching, model/effort forwarding, declared tools/transcript/options reuse, structural auth/unavailable error mapping, existing resume/create fallback, Cursor assign parsing. Update thread-session-factory.spec.ts's unconditional ACP refusal and assign-parser-thread.spec.ts's Cursor refusal; native tests must not call ACP. ACP opens bypass nativeModels() membership checks. Out: discovery and dependency installation (US-002), mode/profile behavior and mode parser (US-006). Any sandbox for ACP agents: they run unsandboxed on the runner host in every mode, as in `nax chat` (user ruling). Per-turn time limits beyond the existing `turnTimeoutSeconds` 900; an approval left waiting longer ends with the turn. The cost cap applies to reported usage only, and an ACP agent that reports no usage counts as zero.

**Interface** — `ThreadSessionFactory.open(input: OpenThreadSessionOptions): Promise<OpenThreadSessionResult>`; `OpenThreadSessionOptions { jobId; thread: ThreadAssign; worktree; tools: CreateAgentSessionOptions['tools']; approvalTimeoutSec }`. Existing result shape: `{ ok: true; session: AgentSession; resumed: boolean } | { ok: false; reason: ThreadFailReason }`; the successful-open criterion checks the ok discriminator, not exact equality with a one-field object. It maps `AGENT_SESSION_AUTH_REQUIRED` to `agent_not_logged_in` and `AGENT_SESSION_BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE` to `backend_unavailable` and resumes with `resumeAgentSession`, falling back to `createAgentSession` on `AGENT_SESSION_NOT_FOUND`. Preserve the current SESSION_EXISTS fallback too.

**Verification** — Use injected ACP/native factories and fake sessions to assert exact backend options, tools and workdir, native isolation, failure mapping, resume behavior and Cursor assign parsing without starting a real ACP binary.

userStories.title: Thread mode stored, permissioned, placed and carried to the runner
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Persist per-thread and per-turn mode, permission REPO ask/full creation, and negotiate mode-capable placement.

**Motivation** — To get code changes a person must dispatch a fleet RUN.

**Approach** — Profile mapping `read` → `read`, `ask` → `ask`, `full` → `full`, native and ACP alike. `mode` lives on `ChatThread` and is snapshotted onto each `FleetThreadTurn`; `findThreadAssign` carries the turn's mode. Creating a REPO thread with `ask`/`full` passes `alsoKeys: [<mode key>]` to the create gate and the service checks the key (`permissions.can`) against the thread's project.

`thread.mode.` joins `HIGH_RISK_PREFIXES`, so both keys are high risk: approvable, floor `none`, default `agent` (an agent waits for approval by default, a human acts directly), like other high-risk keys. The mode is not re-checked on every message: a thread keeps its mode until someone changes it (see Out of Scope).

Prisma `ChatThread` gains `mode String @default("read")` and `pendingApprovals Json?`; `FleetThreadTurn` gains `mode String @default("read")`. Migration `20261124090000_thread_modes` also appends `thread.mode.ask` to the stored `permissions` of the existing `developer` role when absent (precedent `migrations/20261106090000_approval_fleet_core/migration.sql:4-8`).

The create normalisers in `apps/api/src/fleet/threads/thread-input.ts`: the normalised result carries `mode` only for REPO (`read` when absent); `mode` `ask`/`full` on PROJECT or WORKSPACE is a validation error naming `mode`. `parseCapabilities` keeps `threadModes` only when exactly `true`. `PlacementThread` gains `mode`, filled from the thread assign by both builders in `placement.service.ts`; a SESSION job whose mode is `ask` or `full` needs `runner.capabilities.threadModes === true`, else misfit `thread_modes`. `MisfitReason`, `MISFIT_REASONS` and the `PlacementMisfitDto` enum gain `thread_modes`.

**Scope** — In: protocol mode/capability/session_started fields, runtime mirrors, schema and migration, role seed and guarded developer backfill, catalog keys/risk and temporary PENDING_SURFACE_KEYS, REPO create gate and service authorization, domain/repository/DTO maps, mode snapshots for all turns and findThreadAssign, both placement builders and misfit consumers, regenerated OpenAPI and CLI client. Update role-matrix cell count 227 to 229 and regenerate its snapshot; catalog mirrors, pending contract set and fleet-openapi misfit pin; REPO normalizer expectations gain read, PROJECT/WORKSPACE omit mode. Out: mode PATCH and removal of pending exemptions (US-005), runner execution/reporting (US-006), approval ingest using the new JSON column (US-007), web selects (US-011). Re-checking the mode key on every message: a thread keeps its mode after its creator loses `thread.mode.full`, and an any-row `thread.message.send` holder may message an `ask`/`full` thread without holding the mode key.

**Interface** — New `ThreadMode = 'read' | 'ask' | 'full'` in `threads.ts`; `ThreadAssign` gains `mode?: ThreadMode` (absent = `read`). `RunnerCapabilities` gains `threadModes?: true`. `ThreadRunnerLine` `session_started` variant gains `mode?: ThreadMode`. `ThreadDto` gains `mode: ThreadMode`; `CreateThreadDto` gains optional `mode`. Service-level key check: `this.permissions.can(principal, key, { projectId })`. Both new mode keys are non-ownable, project scope, high risk, approval `{ approvable: true, floor: 'none', default: 'agent' }`. US-004 lists both mode keys in `PENDING_SURFACE_KEYS` (the create route only names them through `alsoKeys`, which is not a declaration); US-005 removes them in the change that declares them on the mode route.

**Verification** — Strict security TDD: catalog/placement/parser unit specs plus DB-backed create, permission/approval replay, migration and immutable-turn snapshot scenarios. Regenerate Prisma and API/CLI contracts through repository commands, never hand-edit generated clients. Preserve read behavior for old rows/runners.

userStories.title: Change a thread's mode between turns
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add an approval-gated REPO mode endpoint that atomically changes mode between turns and closes idle sessions for a profiled resume.

**Motivation** — To get code changes a person must dispatch a fleet RUN.

**Approach** — `PATCH /projects/:slug/threads/:id/mode` declares `@Requires(['thread.mode.ask', 'thread.mode.full', 'thread.cap.update'], { mode: 'any', enforcedBy: 'service' })`; the controller validates the body and gates with the key of the TARGET mode (`read` → `thread.cap.update`), and the route command `rest:threads.mode` is registered under all three keys. There is no WORKSPACE mode route: WORKSPACE threads are always `read`. The caller must also be the thread's creator or hold an any-row `thread.cap.update`. A change is refused with 409 when `sendRefusalFor` answers `turnRunning` (a turn is QUEUED, ASSIGNED or running) or a PUBLISH/DISCARD job is active (`threads.busy`); `closing` (a THREAD_CLOSE already queued) still changes the mode without a second command; an idle live SESSION job gets one `THREAD_CLOSE` in the same transaction, so the next message starts a turn that resumes the same session id with the new profile. The change writes a system message (role `system`, status `complete`, content `Mode changed from <from> to <to> by <display name>`, the name resolved when written) and an audit entry.

`threadAuditKey` takes no key; the mode change records its audit entry with `audit.record` directly under the target mode's gate key. Every catalog key must be declared by a route, tool or system writer, or it is reported as `unused-key`, unless it is listed in `PENDING_SURFACE_KEYS`; a listed key that some route declares is reported as `pending-key-declared`. US-005 removes both mode keys from `PENDING_SURFACE_KEYS` in the change that declares them on the mode route.

**Scope** — In: target-mode body validation, controller/service/repository contract, triple-key command registration, creator-or-any-row check in replayable execution, same-transaction mode/message/audit/close writes with job-before-thread locking, no-op response and refusal i18n, catalog exemption removal, OpenAPI/CLI regeneration. Controller-key tests gain the mode handler with mode any/enforcedBy service; approval OpenAPI and permission integration gated-route counts grow 131 to 132. Out: mode storage and creation (US-004), runner profile handling (US-006), decision endpoints (US-008), UI (US-012). `ask` and `full` on PROJECT and WORKSPACE threads: those kinds have no worktree or publish and stay `read`. Changing a thread's agent (backend) after creation; only the mode changes.

**Interface** — `PATCH /projects/:slug/threads/:id/mode` body `{ mode }`; `@Requires(['thread.mode.ask', 'thread.mode.full', 'thread.cap.update'], { mode: 'any', enforcedBy: 'service' })`; route command `rest:threads.mode` registered under `thread.mode.ask`, `thread.mode.full`, `thread.cap.update`; target key mapping `read` → `thread.cap.update`, `ask` → `thread.mode.ask`, `full` → `thread.mode.full`. Current-mode requests return 200 with no system message and no command. Errors are 400 naming mode, 403 for denied target/ownership, 409 threads.turnRunning or threads.busy for active work.

**Verification** — Use the existing gated project thread and permission integration fixtures to prove policy deferral/replay, all owner/target combinations, queued/running versus idle/closing session states, PUBLISH/DISCARD refusals and transactional message/command/audit behavior. Resolve display names at write time and emit live changes/wakes only after commit.

userStories.title: Runner opens sessions in the thread's mode
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Execute every thread turn using its snapshotted mode and advertise runner support for mode execution.
